item.title: Washington D.C. ready and set for historic IndyCar race
item.description: For the first time in America's 250 year history, IndyCar drivers will zoom down some of the nation's most famous streets this weekend. The drivers face new challenges on an unconventional route.

item.title: Top California negotiator on federal proposal to manage Colorado River water
item.description: Western states have long disputed how to split the Colorado River's water. JB Hamby, California's top negotiator, weighs in on the new federal proposal to manage the resource.
item.content:encoded: Western states have long disputed how to split the Colorado River's water. JB Hamby, California's top negotiator, weighs in on the new federal proposal to manage the resource.

item.title: Trump administration's 75-country visa ban was illegal, judge rules
item.description: The U.S. stopped issuing visas for citizens of 75 countries because it said they were likely to need public assistance. A judge ruled the policy illegally discriminated on the basis of nationality.

item.title: Colorado River crisis: Lower basin braces for massive federal water cuts
item.description: The Trump Administration has released a two-year operating plan for the Colorado River. Arizona, California and Nevada are expected to cut their water use from the river.

item.title: As Flock battles public scrutiny, other police surveillance companies see an opening
item.description: Dozens of cities have canceled their contracts with Flock. Some are switching to other companies, but privacy experts say they're no better than Flock.

item.title: President Trump is set to wave the green flag at a historic Indy car race in DC
item.description: We look at the upcoming IndyCar race in Washington, D.C., this weekend, as well as the U.S. Supreme Court decision on the construction of President Trump's White House ballroom.

item.title: Andrew Jackson's plantation revamps tour as critics push for deeper reform
item.description: The tour of President Andrew Jackson's plantation was revamped this year to focus on the life of the 300 people he enslaved. But some people say more needs to be done for their descendants.

item.title: Hours after U.S. imposes tariffs, Canada says it'll strike back starting Sept. 8
item.description: The U.S. has now imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will match those tariffs "dollar for dollar" next month.
